findings.evidence: Identical two-line scripts at lines 109-110, 119-120 and 129-130; `toReal_mul_weight` (line 81) is already the pointwise version, so only the a.e. wrapper is duplicated.
findings.fix: State it once, e.g. `theorem toReal_smul_weight_ae_eq (hg_top : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x < ∞) (hfg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x = 0 → f x = 0) : (fun x => (g x).toReal • weight f g x) =ᵐ[μ] f`, and use it in all three proofs (the third already names it `hfg'`).
findings.issue: The a.e. identity `(fun x => (g x).toReal • weight f g x) =ᵐ[μ] f` is re-proved verbatim three times: lines 108-110 (`integral_weight`), 118-120 (`integrable_weight_iff`), 128-130 (`withDensityᵥ_weight`), each as `filter_upwards [hg_top, hfg] with x hx hx0; rw [smul_eq_mul, toReal_mul_weight hx.ne hx0]`.

findings.evidence: Lines 158-160 and 171-173 are character-for-character identical; grep for `IsProbabilityMeasure \(.*\.withDensity` in ./upstream/mathlib returns nothing.
findings.fix: Extract `theorem isProbabilityMeasure_withDensity (hg1 : ∫⁻ x, g x ∂μ = 1) : IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.withDensity g)` (and either a `lt_top` companion or a single `have` bundle) and call it from both theorems.
findings.issue: `IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.withDensity g)` from `hg1 : ∫⁻ x, g x ∂μ = 1`, and `hg_top` from the same hypothesis, are derived verbatim twice (lines 158-160 and 171-173). Mathlib has no such lemma (no `IsProbabilityMeasure (_.withDensity _)` result anywhere in ./upstream/mathlib), so this is a genuinely reusable fact hidden inside two proofs.

findings.evidence: Line 98; `weight_def` (line 67) is the pointwise `rfl` lemma, and `funext (weight_def f g)` is the ad-hoc way of getting the function-level one.
findings.fix: Add `theorem weight_eq (f : α → ℝ) (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) : weight f g = fun x => f x / (g x).toReal := rfl` next to `weight_def` and start the proof with `rw [weight_eq]`.
findings.issue: `rw [show weight f g = fun x => f x / (g x).toReal from funext (weight_def f g)]` unfolds the definition inline through a `show ... from`, with no comment on why the goal cannot be reached otherwise; the function-level unfolding equation is a fact the rest of the file will want too.

summary: Proofs are short and mostly robust, but three blocks of reasoning are repeated verbatim across theorems instead of being stated as reusable lemmas, and one measurability proof unfolds `weight` through an undocumented `show ... from funext`.
